sanskrit: kumāragurave nityaṃ nīlagrīvāya vedhase vilohitāya dhūmrāya vyādhāyānaparājite
english: Ever to the teacher of Kumāra, to the blue-throated, to the ordainer, to the deep-red one, to the smoke-hued, to the hunter, to the unvanquished.

sanskrit: nityaṃ nīlaśikhaṇḍāya śūline divyacakṣuṣe hantre goptre trinetrāya vyādhāya vasuretase
english: Ever to the dark-crested one, to the bearer of the trident, to the one of divine sight, to the slayer, to the protector, to the three-eyed, to the hunter, to him whose seed is the Vasus.

sanskrit: acintyāyāmbikābhartre sarvadevastutāya ca vṛṣadhvajāya piṅgāya jaṭine brahmacāriṇe
english: To the inconceivable, to the husband of Ambikā, to him praised by all the gods, to him whose banner bears the bull, to the tawny one, to the matted-haired, to the chaste celibate.

sanskrit: tapyamānāya salile brahmaṇyāyājitāya ca viśvātmane viśvasṛje viśvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhate
english: To him who performs austerities within the waters, to the friend of the brahmans, to the unconquered, to the soul of the universe, to the maker of the universe, to him who stands enveloping all that is.

sanskrit: namo namas te sevyāya bhūtānāṃ prabhave sadā brahmavaktrāya śarvāya śaṃkarāya śivāya ca
english: Homage, homage to you, the worshipful, ever the source of all beings, to him from whose mouth issues the Veda, to Śarva, to Śaṃkara, and to Śiva.

sanskrit: namo 'stu vācaspataye prajānāṃ pataye namaḥ namo viśvasya pataye mahatāṃ pataye namaḥ
english: Homage be to the lord of speech; homage to the lord of creatures; homage to the lord of all that is; homage to the lord of the great ones.

sanskrit: namaḥ sahasraśirase sahasrabhujamanyave sahasranetrapādāya namo 'saṃkhyeyakarmaṇe
english: Homage to the thousand-headed, to him whose thousand arms hold fury, to him of a thousand eyes and feet, homage to him whose deeds are beyond number.

sanskrit: namo hiraṇyavarṇāya hiraṇyakavacāya ca bhaktānukampine nityaṃ sidhyatāṃ nau varaḥ prabho
english: Homage to the golden-hued, to him clad in golden armor, to him who ever shows compassion to his devotees: may our boon be granted, O Lord.

sanskrit: evaṃ stutvā mahādevaṃ vāsudevaḥ sahārjunaḥ prasādayām āsa bhavaṃ tadā hy astropalabdhaye
english: Having thus praised Mahādeva, Vāsudeva together with Arjuna then propitiated Bhava, that they might obtain the weapon.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ prītamanā vavande vṛṣabhadhvajam dadarśotphullanayanaḥ samastaṃ tejasāṃ nidhim
english: Then Arjuna, his heart gladdened, bowed to him whose banner bears the bull; with eyes wide in wonder he beheld him, the whole treasury of all splendors.

sanskrit: taṃ copahāraṃ svakṛtaṃ naiśaṃ naityakam ātmanaḥ dadarśa tryambakābhyāśe vāsudevaniveditam
english: And he saw, set before the three-eyed god, the nightly offering that was his own daily rite, presented there by Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tato 'bhipūjya manasā śarvaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ icchāmy ahaṃ divyam astram ity abhāṣata śaṃkaram
english: Then the Pāṇḍava, having worshipped Śarva and Kṛṣṇa in his mind, said to Śaṃkara, "I desire the divine weapon."

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthasya vijñāya varārthe vacanaṃ prabhuḥ vāsudevārjunau devaḥ smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Then the Lord, the god, perceiving Pārtha's words spoken to seek the boon, addressed Vāsudeva and Arjuna with a smile.

sanskrit: saro 'mṛtamayaṃ divyam abhyāśe śatrusūdanau tatra me tad dhanur divyaṃ śaraś ca nihitaḥ purā
english: "There is a divine lake of ambrosia close at hand, O slayers of foes; there long ago I placed that divine bow of mine, and the arrow.

sanskrit: yena devārayaḥ sarve mayā yudhi nipātitāḥ tata ānīyatāṃ kṛṣṇau saśaraṃ dhanur uttamam
english: With it I struck down in battle all the enemies of the gods. Let that supreme bow with its arrow be fetched from there, O you two Kṛṣṇas."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu tau vīrau taṃ śarvaṃ pārṣadaiḥ saha prasthitau tat saro divyaṃ divyāścaryaśatair vṛtam
english: Saying "So be it" to Śarva, who stood among his attendants, the two heroes set out for that divine lake, ringed about by a hundred wondrous marvels.

sanskrit: nirdiṣṭaṃ yad vṛṣāṅkena puṇyaṃ sarvārthasādhakam taj jagmatur asaṃbhrāntau naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī
english: To that holy lake which the bull-marked god had pointed out, accomplisher of every aim, the two sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa went, undismayed.

sanskrit: tatas tu tat saro gatvā sūryamaṇḍalasaṃnibham nāgam antarjale ghoraṃ dadṛśāte 'rjunācyutau
english: Then, reaching that lake which shone like the orb of the sun, Arjuna and Acyuta beheld a dreadful serpent within the waters.

sanskrit: dvitīyaṃ cāparaṃ nāgaṃ sahasraśirasaṃ varam vamantaṃ vipulāṃ jvālāṃ dadṛśāte 'gnivarcasam
english: And they beheld a second serpent, another excellent one with a thousand heads, vomiting forth vast flame and blazing like fire.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇaś ca pārthaś ca saṃspṛśyāpaḥ kṛtāñjalī tau nāgāv upatasthāte namasyantau vṛṣadhvajam
english: Then Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha touched the water and, with hands joined, approached those two serpents, doing homage to him whose banner bears the bull.

sanskrit: gṛṇantau vedaviduṣau tad brahma śatarudriyam aprameyaṃ praṇamantau gatvā sarvātmanā bhavam
english: Learned in the Veda, the two reciting the immeasurable sacred hymn, the Śatarudriya, drew near and bowed to Bhava with their whole being.

sanskrit: tatas tau rudramāhātmyād dhitvā rūpaṃ mahoragau dhanur bāṇaś ca śatrughnaṃ tad dvaṃdvaṃ samapadyata
english: Then, through the majesty of Rudra, those two mighty serpents cast off their forms, and that pair became a bow and an arrow, destroyers of foes.

sanskrit: tato jagṛhatuḥ prītau dhanur bāṇaṃ ca suprabham ājahratur mahātmānau dadatuś ca mahātmane
english: Then the two great-souled ones, well pleased, took up the bow and the bright arrow, carried them back, and gave them to the great-souled god.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārśvād vṛṣāṅkasya brahmacārī nyavartata piṅgākṣas tapasaḥ kṣetraṃ balavān nīlalohitaḥ
english: Then from the side of the bull-marked god there came forth a celibate ascetic, tawny-eyed, a very field of austerity, mighty, dark-red of hue.

sanskrit: sa tad gṛhya dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ tasthau sthānaṃ samāhitaḥ vyakarṣac cāpi vidhivat saśaraṃ dhanur uttamam
english: Taking up that finest of bows, he stood in his stance with collected mind, and drew the supreme bow with its arrow according to the rule.

sanskrit: tasya maurvīṃ ca muṣṭiṃ ca sthānaṃ cālakṣya pāṇḍavaḥ śrutvā mantraṃ bhavaproktaṃ jagrāhācintyavikramaḥ
english: Marking his bowstring, his grip, and his stance, and hearing the spell spoken by Bhava, the Pāṇḍava of inconceivable valor grasped it all.

sanskrit: sarasy eva ca taṃ bāṇaṃ mumocātibalaḥ prabhuḥ cakāra ca punar vīras tasmin sarasi tad dhanuḥ
english: And into the lake itself the mighty lord loosed that arrow, and again the hero placed the bow back within that lake.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītaṃ bhavaṃ jñātvā smṛtimān arjunas tadā varam āraṇyakaṃ dattaṃ darśanaṃ śaṃkarasya ca manasā cintayām āsa tan me saṃpadyatām iti
english: Then Arjuna, mindful and aware that Bhava was pleased, recalled in his heart the boon granted him in the forest and the vision of Śaṃkara, and thought, "May that come to fulfillment for me."

sanskrit: tasya tan matam ājñāya prītaḥ prādād varaṃ bhavaḥ tac ca pāśupataṃ ghoraṃ pratijñāyāś ca pāraṇam
english: Knowing his intent, Bhava, well pleased, granted him the boon—that dread Pāśupata weapon, and the means to fulfill his vow.

sanskrit: saṃhṛṣṭaromā durdharṣaḥ kṛtaṃ kāryam amanyata vavandatuś ca saṃhṛṣṭau śirobhyāṃ tau maheśvaram
english: Thrilled to the roots of his hair, the unassailable one deemed his task accomplished; and the two, full of joy, bowed their heads to Maheśvara.

sanskrit: anujñātau kṣaṇe tasmin bhavenārjunakeśavau prāptau svaśibiraṃ vīrau mudā paramayā yutau indrāviṣṇū yathā prītau jambhasya vadhakāṅkṣiṇau
english: Granted leave at that moment by Bhava, Arjuna and Keśava, those two heroes, reached their own camp filled with the highest joy, as glad as Indra and Viṣṇu eager to slay Jambha.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tayoḥ saṃvadator eva kṛṣṇadārukayos tadā sātyagād rajanī rājann atha rājānvabudhyata
english: Saṃjaya said: While the two, Kṛṣṇa and Dāruka, were yet conversing, the night passed away, O king, and then the king awoke.

sanskrit: paṭhanti pāṇisvanikā māgadhā madhuparkikāḥ vaitālikāś ca sūtāś ca tuṣṭuvuḥ puruṣarṣabham
english: Hand-clapping musicians, bards of Magadha, those who bear the honeyed welcome-draught, panegyrists, and charioteer-minstrels recited and sang the praises of that bull among men.

sanskrit: nartakāś cāpy anṛtyanta jagur gītāni gāyakāḥ kuruvaṃśastavārthāni madhuraṃ raktakaṇṭhinaḥ
english: Dancers too danced, and singers of sweet and ardent voice sang songs whose burden was the glory of the Kuru line.

sanskrit: mṛdaṅgā jharjharā bheryaḥ paṇavānakagomukhāḥ āḍambarāś ca śaṅkhāś ca dundubhyaś ca mahāsvanāḥ
english: Tabors, jharjharas, kettledrums, small drums and large drums and cow-horn pipes, war-drums and conch-shells and deep-voiced great drums—

sanskrit: evam etāni sarvāṇi tathānyāny api bhārata vādayanti sma saṃhṛṣṭāḥ kuśalāḥ sādhuśikṣitāḥ
english: all these, O Bhārata, and yet other instruments besides, were sounded with delight by skilled and well-trained players.

sanskrit: sa meghasamanirghoṣo mahāñ śabdo 'spṛśad divam pārthivapravaraṃ suptaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram abodhayat
english: That great sound, roaring like a thundercloud, touched the heavens and roused the sleeping Yudhiṣṭhira, foremost of kings.

sanskrit: pratibuddhaḥ sukhaṃ supto mahārhe śayanottame utthāyāvaśyakāryārthaṃ yayau snānagṛhaṃ tataḥ
english: Awakened, having slept at ease upon his costly and excellent couch, he rose and went thence to the bath-house to perform his needful duties.

sanskrit: tataḥ śuklāmbarāḥ snātās taruṇāṣṭottaraṃ śatam snāpakāḥ kāñcanaiḥ kumbhaiḥ pūrṇaiḥ samupatasthire
english: Then a hundred and eight young attendants for the bath, clad in white and freshly washed, drew near with golden jars filled with water.

sanskrit: bhadrāsane sūpaviṣṭaḥ paridhāyāmbaraṃ laghu sasnau candanasaṃyuktaiḥ pānīyair abhimantritaiḥ
english: Seated well upon an auspicious seat, wearing a light garment, he bathed in waters charged with sandal and hallowed by sacred chants.

sanskrit: utsāditaḥ kaṣāyeṇa balavadbhiḥ suśikṣitaiḥ āplutaḥ sādhivāsena jalena ca sugandhinā
english: He was rubbed with astringent paste by strong, well-trained men, and bathed with perfumed water steeped in sweet-scented herbs.

sanskrit: hariṇā candanenāṅgam anulipya mahābhujaḥ sragvī cākliṣṭavasanaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitaḥ
english: Having anointed his body with yellow sandal, the great-armed one, garlanded and clad in spotless raiment, stood facing east with hands joined in reverence.

sanskrit: jajāpa japyaṃ kaunteyaḥ satāṃ mārgam anuṣṭhitaḥ tato 'gniśaraṇaṃ dīptaṃ praviveśa vinītavat
english: The son of Kuntī murmured the prayer fit for muttering, following the path of the good, and then humbly entered the blazing chamber of the sacred fire.

sanskrit: samiddhaṃ sa pavitrābhir agnim āhutibhis tathā mantrapūtābhir arcitvā niścakrāma gṛhāt tataḥ
english: Having worshipped the kindled fire with pure oblations hallowed by sacred formulas, he then came forth from the chamber.

sanskrit: dvitīyāṃ puruṣavyāghraḥ kakṣyāṃ niṣkramya pārthivaḥ tatra vedavido viprān apaśyad brāhmaṇarṣabhān
english: Passing into the second courtyard, that tiger among men, the king, beheld there brahmans versed in the Veda, bulls among the twice-born.

sanskrit: dāntān vedavratasnātān snātān avabhṛtheṣu ca sahasrānucarān saurān aṣṭau daśaśatāni ca
english: Self-controlled, bathed in the vows of the Veda and in the final ablutions of sacrifice, devotees of the sun attended by thousands—eight thousand of them, and a thousand more.

sanskrit: akṣataiḥ sumanobhiś ca vācayitvā mahābhujaḥ tān dvijān madhusarpirbhyāṃ phalaiḥ śreṣṭhaiḥ sumaṅgalaiḥ
english: Having had them pronounce blessings with whole grains and flowers, the great-armed one honored those twice-born with honey and clarified butter and with choice and auspicious fruits.

sanskrit: prādāt kāñcanam ekaikaṃ niṣkaṃ viprāya pāṇḍavaḥ alaṃkṛtaṃ cāśvaśataṃ vāsāṃsīṣṭāś ca dakṣiṇāḥ
english: The Pāṇḍava gave to each brahman a golden coin, and a hundred caparisoned horses, garments, and the gifts they wished as sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: tathā gāḥ kapilā dogdhrīḥ sarṣabhāḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ hemaśṛṅgī rūpyakhurā dattvā cakre pradakṣiṇam
english: The son of Pāṇḍu likewise gave tawny milk-cows together with their bulls, their horns gilded and their hooves shod with silver, and walked round them in reverence.

sanskrit: svastikān vardhamānāṃś ca nandyāvartāṃś ca kāñcanān mālyaṃ ca jalakumbhāṃś ca jvalitaṃ ca hutāśanam
english: Golden svastikas and vardhamānas and nandyāvarta emblems, garlands and water-jars, and the blazing fire that bears the oblations;

sanskrit: pūrṇāny akṣatapātrāṇi rucakān rocanāṃs tathā svalaṃkṛtāḥ śubhāḥ kanyā dadhisarpirmadhūdakam
english: vessels filled with whole grains, ornaments and yellow pigment, and fair, well-adorned maidens bearing curds, ghee, honey, and water—

sanskrit: maṅgalyān pakṣiṇaś caiva yac cānyad api pūjitam dṛṣṭvā spṛṣṭvā ca kaunteyo bāhyāṃ kakṣyām agāt tataḥ
english: auspicious birds too, and whatever else is held holy—all these the son of Kuntī beheld and touched, and then passed on to the outer courtyard.

sanskrit: tatas tasya mahābāhos tiṣṭhataḥ paricārakāḥ sauvarṇaṃ sarvatobhadraṃ muktāvaiḍūryamaṇḍitam
english: Then, as that great-armed one stood there, his attendants brought a golden throne, auspicious on every side, adorned with pearls and cat's-eye gems—

sanskrit: parārdhyāstaraṇāstīrṇaṃ sottaracchadam ṛddhimat viśvakarmakṛtaṃ divyam upajahrur varāsanam
english: spread with priceless coverings, furnished with a canopy above, opulent and divine, fashioned by Viśvakarman—that finest of seats they brought forth.

sanskrit: tatra tasyopaviṣṭasya bhūṣaṇāni mahātmanaḥ upajahrur mahārhāṇi preṣyāḥ śubhrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: When the great-souled one was seated there, the servants brought him costly ornaments, gleaming and bright in every part.

sanskrit: yuktābharaṇaveṣasya kaunteyasya mahātmanaḥ rūpam āsīn mahārāja dviṣatāṃ śokavardhanam
english: When the great-souled son of Kuntī was fitted with ornament and array, his form, O great king, was such as to swell the grief of his foes.

sanskrit: pāṇḍaraiś candraraśmyābhair hemadaṇḍaiś ca cāmaraiḥ dodhūyamānaḥ śuśubhe vidyudbhir iva toyadaḥ
english: Fanned with white yak-tail whisks gleaming like moonbeams and set on golden handles, he shone like a rain-cloud lit by flashes of lightning.

sanskrit: saṃstūyamānaḥ sūtaiś ca vandyamānaś ca bandibhiḥ upagīyamāno gandharvair āste sma kurunandanaḥ
english: Extolled by minstrels, lauded by panegyrists, and hymned by gandharvas, the joy of the Kurus sat enthroned.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād āsīt tu bandināṃ nisvano mahān nemighoṣaś ca rathināṃ khuraghoṣaś ca vājinām
english: Then, within a moment, there arose a great clamor of bards, the rumble of chariot-wheel rims, and the clatter of horses' hooves.

sanskrit: hrādena gajaghaṇṭānāṃ śaṅkhānāṃ ninadena ca narāṇāṃ padaśabdaiś ca kampatīva sma medinī
english: With the jangle of elephant-bells, the blare of conches, and the tread of men's feet, the very earth seemed to tremble.

sanskrit: tataḥ śuddhāntam āsādya jānubhyāṃ bhūtale sthitaḥ śirasā vandanīyaṃ tam abhivandya jagatpatim
english: Then a man, reaching the inner apartments, knelt with both knees upon the ground and bowed his head to that lord of men, worthy of homage.

sanskrit: kuṇḍalī baddhanistriṃśaḥ saṃnaddhakavaco yuvā abhipraṇamya śirasā dvāḥstho dharmātmajāya vai nyavedayad dhṛṣīkeśam upayātaṃ mahātmane
english: A youth, earringed, his sword girded on, his armor fastened, a doorkeeper, bowing his head to the son of Dharma, announced to that great-souled one that Hṛṣīkeśa had arrived.

sanskrit: so 'bravīt puruṣavyāghraḥ svāgatenaiva mādhavam arghyaṃ caivāsanaṃ cāsmai dīyatāṃ paramārcitam
english: That tiger among men replied, "Welcome indeed to Mādhava! Let the guest-offering and a seat, held in highest honor, be given to him."

sanskrit: tataḥ praveśya vārṣṇeyam upaveśya varāsane satkṛtya satkṛtas tena paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then, having ushered in the Vārṣṇeya and seated him upon a noble seat, and having honored him and been honored by him in turn, Yudhiṣṭhira made inquiry.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sukhena rajanī vyuṣṭā kaccit te madhusūdana kaccij jñānāni sarvāṇi prasannāni tavācyuta
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Has the night passed pleasantly for you, O slayer of Madhu? And are all your faculties serene, O Acyuta?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vāsudevo 'pi tad yuktaṃ paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiram tataḥ kṣattā prakṛtayo nyavedayad upasthitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Vāsudeva too made fitting inquiry of Yudhiṣṭhira in turn; then the chamberlain announced that the chief subjects had come and were waiting.

sanskrit: anujñātaś ca rājñā sa prāveśayata taṃ janam virāṭaṃ bhīmasenaṃ ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca sātyakim
english: Granted leave by the king, he ushered in those people: Virāṭa and Bhīmasena, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Sātyaki,

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ yamau caiva cekitānaṃ ca kekayān yuyutsuṃ caiva kauravyaṃ pāñcālyaṃ cottamaujasam
english: Śikhaṇḍin and the twins, and Cekitāna and the Kekayas, and Yuyutsu of the Kuru line, and the Pāñcāla Uttamaujas.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriyarṣabham upatasthur mahātmānaṃ viviśuś cāsaneṣu te
english: These and many other warriors approached that great-souled bull among kṣatriyas and took their places upon the seats.

sanskrit: ekasminn āsane vīrāv upaviṣṭau mahābalau kṛṣṇaś ca yuyudhānaś ca mahātmānau mahādyutī
english: Upon a single seat sat two mighty heroes, Kṛṣṇa and Yuyudhāna, great-souled and of great splendor.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiras teṣāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ madhusūdanam abravīt puṇḍarīkākṣam ābhāṣya madhuraṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, in the hearing of them all, addressed the lotus-eyed slayer of Madhu and spoke to him sweet words.

sanskrit: ekaṃ tvāṃ vayam āśritya sahasrākṣam ivāmarāḥ prārthayāmo jayaṃ yuddhe śāśvatāni sukhāni ca
english: "Relying on you alone, as the immortals rely on the thousand-eyed Indra, we pray for victory in battle and for lasting happiness.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi rājyavināśaṃ ca dviṣadbhiś ca nirākriyām kleśāṃś ca vividhān kṛṣṇa sarvāṃs tān api vettha naḥ
english: For you, Kṛṣṇa, know all our sufferings—the ruin of our kingdom, the humiliation at the hands of our foes, and our manifold afflictions.

sanskrit: tvayi sarveśa sarveṣām asmākaṃ bhaktavatsala sukham āyattam atyarthaṃ yātrā ca madhusūdana
english: In you, O lord of all, O lover of your devotees, the welfare of us all utterly depends, and our very course of action too, O slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: sa tathā kuru vārṣṇeya yathā tvayi mano mama arjunasya yathā satyā pratijñā syāc cikīrṣitā
english: Therefore act, O Vārṣṇeya, in accord with my trust in you, so that Arjuna's vow, which he longs to fulfill, may come true.

sanskrit: sa bhavāṃs tārayatv asmād duḥkhāmarṣamahārṇavāt pāraṃ titīrṣatām adya plavo no bhava mādhava
english: May you carry us across this vast ocean of sorrow and indignation; be this day our raft, O Mādhava, for we long to reach the farther shore.

sanskrit: na hi tat kurute saṃkhye kārtavīryasamas tv api rathī yat kurute kṛṣṇa sārathir yatnam āsthitaḥ
english: For even a chariot-warrior the equal of Kārtavīrya cannot accomplish in battle, O Kṛṣṇa, what a charioteer who sets himself to the effort can accomplish."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca sāmareṣv api lokeṣu sarveṣu na tathāvidhaḥ śarāsanadharaḥ kaś cid yathā pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: In all the worlds, even with their gods, there is no bowman of such a kind as Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: vīryavān astrasaṃpannaḥ parākrānto mahābalaḥ yuddhaśauṇḍaḥ sadāmarṣī tejasā paramo nṛṇām
english: Valiant, accomplished in weapons, daring, of mighty strength, eager for battle, ever impatient of insult, in splendor the foremost of men—

sanskrit: sa yuvā vṛṣabhaskandho dīrghabāhur mahābalaḥ siṃharṣabhagatiḥ śrīmān dviṣatas te haniṣyati
english: that youth, bull-shouldered, long-armed, of mighty strength, with the gait of a lion and a bull, glorious—he shall slay your foes.
